control_flow: avoidWalls: if the right light is below 60 %, decide about obstacles; otherwise call driveInTheDark.
In dim light: if the front obstacle sensor sees something, turn left 15°; else if the left one sees something, turn right 15°; else call driveInTheDark.
driveInTheDark: if the left light is below 70 %, drive forward at 30 % without a distance; otherwise call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if the front obstacle sensor sees something, stop; otherwise call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left (10/40); otherwise curve right (40/10).

uncertainties: You only spoke about the tunnel: your program also follows a line and stops at walls in bright light, which you didn't describe.
In dim light the program never stops at a wall: it only turns away from it in 15° steps.
A tunnel's wall comes in front of the robot's left or right half; whether a wall ever stands right in front of its front sensor depends on how sharply the tunnel bends.
In a bend to the right the left wall is the one in front of the left half, so the program turns right; a wall it never reads is the one on its right.
